questions.question: Select the most appropriate option of fill in blank No. 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option of fill in blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
Read the sentences properly then only one can understand the passage and choose suitable words for the given blanks.

Since is used to introduce a reason for something.

For eg: Since I am running late, I will be taking a cab.

And is used to join two parts of a sentence, one part happening after the other part.

For eg: I got dressed and had breakfast.

Because is used to give a reason.

For eg: The journey was quite quick because the road was clear.

So is also used to give a reason; therefore

For eg:I was lost so I bought a street map.

In the given blank, it requires a joining word which is "and".

Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 3.
questions.solution:
In the given question, a proper understanding of pronoun is required.

Its is a singular possessive pronoun for non-human objects 

For eg:A plant produces its own food

Their is a possessive pronoun used for: 
a) plural non-human things b) plural humans c) singular humans of unspecified gender: 

For eg: Anyone who hasn't turned off their phone off, please could they do it now.

Few people don't turn off their phones in quiet carriages on the train. 

They is a subject pronoun. It refers to a group of two or more people.

For eg:They all started to rush for the window seat.

Them is an object pronoun. It replaces nouns that are the objects of sentences.

For eg:After lunch, all four of them went outside to play ball.

In the given sentence, it is talking about plural "bodies" so it will be "their".

Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer to fill in the blank number 2 is option 1, "next."

Key Points

  • The word next means coming immediately after the present one in order, rank, or space.

  • "In the very next" is a phrase used to describe something that is happening immediately following the current event or situation. This phrase is often used in temporal and sequential contexts.

  • Here are a few examples:

    • "In the very next chapter of the book, the mystery of the haunted house is revealed."

      • This means that the mystery will be revealed immediately in the following chapter.

    • "In the very next game, the team made a fantastic comeback."

      • This implies that the team had a great performance in the game immediately after the current one.

  • In the context of the passage, the word next indicates that the very next entry in the diary shows a major gap in time and events from the previous one. 
  • Hence, "next," is the most appropriate choice for filling in the blank number 2 in this sentence.

Additional Information

  • Option 2, "former," would not make sense in this context as it refers to something that was previously in a certain state or position. For example, "My former boss was very strict."
  • Option 3, "earlier," could work in this sentence, but it would change the meaning slightly. It would imply that the meeting was originally scheduled for a later date but has been moved up.  For example, "I was supposed to meet with my boss next week, but we moved it to an earlier date."
  • Option 4, "over," would not make sense in this context as it means to be finished or concluded. For example, "The meeting is over, and we can all go home now."
  •  Next (अगला) - Coming immediately after the time or order in consideration.
    • Example: The next meeting is scheduled for Monday.
  • Former (पूर्व) - Occurring in the past or before the present time; previous.
    • Example: The former president visited his old school.
  • Earlier (पहले) - Happening or done before a particular time.
    • Example: If only she had known about it earlier.
  • Over (समाप्त) - Finished; concluded.
    • Example: The match was over within a couple of hours.

The word "who" is used as the subject of a sentence or clause, and it refers to a person. In this case, the sentence is likely asking for the subject of a verb or the person who is performing an action. For example, "Who is going to the party?" or "Who wrote this book?"

Option 2, "whose," is used to show possession or ownership. For example, "Whose car is this?" or "Whose idea was it to go on this trip?"

Option 3, "whom," is used as the object of a sentence or clause, and it refers to a person. For example, "Whom did you invite to the party?" or "To whom should I address this letter?"

Option 4, "which," is used to refer to things or objects. For example, "Which book do you want to read?" or "Which color do you prefer?"

Additional Information:
It's important to note that the use of "whom" is becoming less common in modern English, and many people use "who" instead, even in formal writing. However, in very formal or academic writing, "whom" may still be preferred.
